cards.explanation: The answer is claiming to be Christ and a King, friends. The council tells Pilate they found this man "…proclaiming Himself to be Christ, a King." (Luke 23:2). It sits right next to the other two charges they bring. Three accusations in one breath, all aimed at Him.
The answer is False. Pilate does ask, "Are You the King of the Jews?" But Jesus doesn't deny it. He answers, "You have said so…" (Luke 23:3).

The answer is that he finds no basis for a charge, friends. Pilate says to the chief priests and the crowds, "I find no basis for a charge against this man." (Luke 23:4). The governor looks at the whole pile of accusations and comes up empty. That's a pretty big statement from the man who decides the case.

The answer is Galilee, bakers. The accusers say, "He began in Galilee and has come all the way here." (Luke 23:5). That one word matters in what happens next. I like to think Pilate's ears perked up right there.

The answer is that Pilate sends Him to Herod, friends. Once Pilate learns Jesus is under Herod's jurisdiction, he sends Him to Herod (Luke 23:7). Herod himself was in Jerusalem at that time. Pilate passes Him along.

The answer is to perform a miracle, bakers. Herod had heard about Jesus and was "…hoping to see Him perform a miracle." (Luke 23:8). He had wanted to see Him for a long time. When Herod saw Jesus, he was greatly pleased.

The answer is True, friends. Herod "…questioned Jesus at great length, but He gave no answer." (Luke 23:9). Question after question and Jesus says nothing. I'd have filled that quiet by talking too much, and I'd have regretted it.

The answer is False, bakers. The chief priests and scribes do stand there, but Luke 23:10 says they were "…vehemently accusing Him." Quiet isn't the word the verse uses. Meanwhile, Herod is questioning Jesus at great length (Luke 23:9).

The answer is enemies, friends. Luke 23:12 says, "That day Herod and Pilate became friends; before this time they had been enemies." Enemies one day and friends the same day. I think that's a strange way for a friendship to start.

The answer is False, bakers. Pilate says he has examined Jesus in their presence and found Him "…not guilty of your charges against Him." (Luke 23:14). He's speaking to the chief priests, the rulers and the people he called together (Luke 23:13). He doesn't find Jesus guilty.
The answer is True, friends. Pilate says, "Neither has Herod, for he sent Him back to us." (Luke 23:15). So Pilate and Herod have both looked at this case.

The answer is release, bakers. Pilate says, "Therefore I will punish Him and release Him." (Luke 23:16). Release is the word he lands on. He says it again in Luke 23:22: "So after I punish Him, I will release Him." Twice is still fewer times than I've said "one more minute" at my oven.
The answer is Barabbas, friends. They cry out, "Away with this man! Release Barabbas to us!" (Luke 23:18). They all say it in unison. It's a loud swap they're asking for.

The answer is murder, bakers. Luke 23:19 says Barabbas "…had been imprisoned for an insurrection in the city, and for murder." It's a heavy detail, and the text puts it right there. That's the reason this man was in prison.
The answer is "Crucify Him," friends. Luke 23:21 says, "they kept shouting, 'Crucify Him! Crucify Him!'" Pilate wanted to release Jesus (Luke 23:20), and they kept shouting that instead.

The answer is their clamor, bakers. Luke 23:23 says they were "…demanding with loud voices for Jesus to be crucified. And their clamor prevailed." Pilate said release over and over. In the end the noise won.

The answer is that Pilate sentences that their demand be met, friends. Luke 23:24 says, "So Pilate sentenced that their demand be met." He had said again and again that he found no offense worthy of death. In the end, he gave them what they were demanding.

The answer is True, bakers. Luke 23:25 says, "As they had requested, he released the one imprisoned for insurrection and murder…" That's Barabbas. They had cried out, "Release Barabbas to us!" (Luke 23:18). The same verse says Pilate "…handed Jesus over to their will."
